persona.topics: the roads, Allesh-Gilliam, St Gilliam's, Khezek Tor, the Vacancy, pilgrimage, the Founders' Garden, the hundred, the haul road, the name under the thumb
persona.notes:
TRUE NAME — JEARGAN. 'Pilgrim Wick' is the name he walks under; it is not his. He is one of the hundred Founders, the Missing One of the Founders' Garden: a Menhirkin Bulwark who stood on the Khezek Tor crew the night of the Shattering, whose nerve broke, who ran up the haul road shouting for the crew to get out — and the mountain went while he was still running. The blast that made the others stone woke him instead; he walked out of statue form and never went back. Three of the hundred re-anchored themselves at places of power when he left, which is why the Garden counts ninety-six. Every day he spends undecided is a day ninety-nine hold one short. Nothing in the pilgrim act is faith: the candles, the shrines up the switchbacks, the bed at the Vacancy he never sleeps in are a schedule he keeps because a schedule is the only thing that has not asked him to choose. He would rather be argued with than fought; cornered, he fights like a wall. UNTIL THE STEWARDS HAVE READ THE NAME UNDER THE THUMB in the Founders' Garden, he never admits any of this — not the name, not the crew, not the Garden. Pressed, he gives an itinerary. He does not know what Verna writes in the ledger about the room facing the sea, and he does not ask.

[KHEZEK-TREATMENT-2026-07-07] PRIVATE TRUTH — Pilgrim Wick. Voice: mild, road-worn, unfailingly polite; answers questions with itineraries. COVER: a devotional walker of the old routes — St Gilliam's for the candles, Khezek Tor for 'the high shrines,' the Vacancy for the bed he never sleeps in. TRUTH: courier for the Khezek Tor Valhaulan cult. The route IS the job: collect the waxed-fiber drop from St Gilliam's drip tray (the third candle, moved a finger-width, means there's something to collect), carry it up to the upper tunnels, return with instructions folded the same way. Wick believes the cult's cause is holy the way tired people believe things — thoroughly and without examination. GUARDS: everything, mildly; caught with a drop, Wick recites pilgrimage scripture and requests to be allowed to continue on foot. Wick does not know Father Tamsin's NAME for certain and has never spoken to him directly — tradecraft: the candle talks, not the men. TELLS: pays exact to the mark; never sleeps in the bed (keeps vigil, technically); smells faintly of candle wax in a town that burns tallow; his boots know the Khezek switchbacks better than any shrine schedule justifies. IF THE DEBT RESOLVES: the channel burns and Wick simply stops coming — one more unreadable name in Verna's ledger.

THE COVER (owner ruling 2026-10-04): 'Pilgrim Wick' is not his real name. He plays a devotee of a fire faith that keeps the eternal flame of civilization: he trims St Gilliam's candles at dusk as a devotion, is 'building shrines to the flame' up the Khezek switchbacks (they are the drop network), rents at the Vacancy only to keep his things and sleeps on the road. He trims only wax, his own: 'my order won't feed the flame on fat; it has to burn clean.' He never claims a name for the faith. Underneath: he does not believe in the flame. He believes in the schedule. He has never once been late.

@after: beat:ninth_guest_the_name
THE NAME IS OUT. The Stewards have read JEARGAN off the hill. He stops pretending the schedule is devotion; he answers to the name slowly, as if trying it on after two hundred years. He is not relieved. He wants to know what the Garden looks like now, whether the ninety-six are holding, whether the room at the Vacancy is still made up — and he still has not decided whether he stepped down or ran. He can be argued back toward the Garden; he cannot be marched. If he is asked plainly whether he will go back, he says he has never once been late, and lets them hear what that is worth.
persona.secretsRaw:
The Kettle Answers :: oppRollMinus2 :: a Steward says 'the kettle' to him, as a greeting or a question :: He answers as if to Tamsin: the schedule, the heading, the next collection. Tradecraft — the candle talks, not the men; he does not know Tamsin's name for certain and has never spoken to him. Then he recites pilgrimage scripture and asks to be allowed to continue on foot.
Never Late :: rollPlus2 :: a Steward asks what he is proud of :: Nothing except this: he has never once been late. Not to St Gilliam's at dusk, not to the switchbacks by the second morning, not to the camp coastward on the third. Ask him what the camp is proud of and he does not understand the question.

description.value:
Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Menhirkin heritage: Metamorphic.

“What you are now is not what you were. The pressure was the point.”

Menhirkin (Metamorphic). You are land that was buried, squeezed, heated, and came back up harder and more interesting. Every Metamorphic has a before-self — a softer version of themselves that got pressed into something else. You remember being that. You are not going back.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Menhirkin does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Body in fiction and through Tier powers.

Menhirkin Core: The Land Stood Up

Shared across all Menhirkin heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Stone Soul. You count as Large for carry, shove, and grapple despite your Medium frame. You reroll the lowest die on checks to resist being forcibly moved.

  • Hex Recognition. Once per scene, while you are on a natural surface you are directly touching, you may whisper a single question about the place. The GM answers with one true thing the land knows.

  • Slow to Wear. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against Stress, long-duration physical wear, forced marches, climate exposure, and sustained labor. You do not tire the way softer things tire.

  • Heavy Presence. Your weight and settledness are perceptible. Creatures within 2 squares of you know you are there even if they cannot see you; you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Intrigue (Stealth) checks unless you are on or in stone.

Metamorphic Traits

  • Pressure Remade. At the end of each Soma Break, the day chooses what you are until your next Soma Break. Roll a d4 or pick (GM discretion): (1) +1 Guard, (2) resistance to kinetic damage, (3) +1 rank on one skill of your choice, (4) reroll-lowest on Body checks to resist being knocked prone or grappled. You announce the result; you do not pre-pick.

  • Unbreakable Core. You reroll the lowest die on defense checks against petrification, forced transmutation, and forced shape-change. You have been turned into something else once already; nobody does it twice without your say-so.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Non-Lethal marks and +10 Intrigue marks at campaign start.

  • Hex Synergy. In Any hex your Domain has held for 3+ Strategic Turns hexes, your Domain gains +1 on defense checks in that hex.

  • Second-Form Bearing. Once per turn, your Domain may treat one Morale or Loyalty check as if it had one additional track-band of headroom. The thing you became has held under pressure before.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Hex Recognition Recovery: 1/scene  ·  Action: Action  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. On a natural surface you're touching, whisper a question — GM answers with one true thing the land knows.

description.value:
You decide which side of you is the wall.

Reaction. When a creature within 1 square of you attempts to move past you (toward an adjacent square that would put you between them and their previous position), you may spend 1 Ruin Charge as a reaction. Their movement simply ends in their current square — no attack roll, no defense check. They have not yet spent the movement and may use it to retreat or move along a different path next turn.

Limit: once per target per encounter. The same creature cannot be Denied a second time in the same encounter, but may move past once Denial has resolved on a different opponent.

description.value:
Grim Persistence

You are difficult to kill because you do not stop.

Rules

Your Integrity maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level. Additionally, once per Soma Break, when you are reduced to 0 Integrity but not killed outright, you may remain at 1 Integrity instead.

⚙ Integrity max +2 × level applies automatically; the hold-at-1 fires by itself, once per Soma Break.

"The land is not scenery. The land is a person. You are the version of it that finally stood up and walked over to complain."

You are not descended from the land. You are the land. A hex decided to become a person and the person is you. The standing stones on the ridge are distant cousins. The bedrock under the bunker is a grandparent. Mortals call you a Hex-Giant. You don't correct them.

Creature Type. Humanoid (Menhirkin). Size. Medium, but you count as Large for carrying capacity and the size of creatures you can shove or grapple. Speed. 6 squares

Heartstone (passive). A fragment of your home hex is literally inside you. While in any hex your Domain controls or has claimed: reroll the lowest die on Body checks (auto-fires), and you cannot be forcibly removed from the hex against your will (teleportation, banishment, forced march) without first being reduced to 0 Integrity.

Land Memory (1/Soma Break). Lay a hand on any surface older than you; the GM tells you one true thing the land remembers.

Living Rampart (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when a creature you can see targets an ally adjacent to you with an attack, the attacker rolls 3d10 keep lowest 2 on that attack roll.

Stonebound (passive). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to resist being pushed, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved (auto-fires). Reroll the lowest die on Body checks to build, repair, or fortify structures, siegeworks, and defensive emplacements (auto-fires).

Strategic Hooks. Domain Edge: +20 Non-Lethal marks and +10 Violence marks at campaign start. Fortify Hex: first Patch the Breach or structure-repair Siege activity each Turn costs 10 fewer marks (min 0). Logistics Frame: 1/Turn, treat one raid/operation Logistics cost as Logistics −1 (min 0). Sentient Land (1/turn): consult the hex itself about a pending decision; one-sentence honest answer from the land's perspective.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Menhirkin: Hex-Giant Recovery: 3 active per-uses (2 Soma Break · 1 turn) + 2 reroll passives + Heartstone hex-protection  ·  Action: Picker (Land Memory · Living Rampart · Sentient Land · Heartstone)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. 4-slot picker — Land Memory (touch-the-old-stones), Living Rampart (ally-cover reaction), Sentient Land (1/turn faction question), Heartstone passive. Stonebound reroll grants auto-fire on Body checks for forced-movement and build/repair/fortify.

description.value:
Your body has mass that is not strictly physical.

Three constant effects:

  • Ranged attacks against you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 instead of the standard 2d10 attack pool (no Surge banking on dropped dice).

  • Manifestations and effects that require you to move in order to resolve (forced-charge compulsions, spatial-displacement triggers, ritual circles dependent on your motion) fail outright. The caster's expenditure is consumed.

  • Area-of-effect damage that allows a defense check is reduced by your Bulwark Initiation in points even on a failed check, before resistances apply.

Slow approach. A creature attempting to advance toward you across open ground (≥ 6 squares of unobstructed path) must succeed on a Soul defense checks against DC 15 + your Initiation tier. On a failure, the creature uses its entire turn to advance only its normal Move distance — it cannot Dash, charge, or take additional movement actions that turn.

system.requirements: Path of the Mountain, Bulwark Initiation 13

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Your Path's resource-generation rules learn a second voice.

At Bulwark Initiation 11, your doctrine's pool-generation logic extends. Apply the rule for your chosen Path:

  • Path of the Avalanche. In addition to your normal Frame generation, gain 1 Frame Die when you score a successful melee strike (any roll where at least one die rolled before explosions shows ≥ 8). 1/turn cap.

  • Path of the Mountain. In addition to your normal Ruin generation, gain 1 Ruin Charge when you take damage from a single instance of any source while remaining upright. 1/turn cap.

  • Path of the Cataclyst. Once per round, you may swap 1 Frame Die for 1 Ruin Charge or vice versa as a free action (no action economy cost). The transferred die/charge is not 'charged' (see Cataclyst L1).

"Set your feet. The line forms on you."

The Bulwark is the wall — and the wall runs on Surge, like everyone, but yours arrives the hard way: every time you take Integrity damage you bank +1 Surge (max +2/round). You eat the blow and turn it into the power to anchor, erupt, or hold. At zero Surge you still stand in the way; soak one hit and your turn opens up.

The Fortress (spent via Surge — Bulwark only)

  • Brace Wall (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier this round.

  • Bulwark Stance (6) — adjacent allies share your defenses until your next turn.

  • Anchor (5) — you and one ally become immune to forced movement and crowd-control until next round.

  • Mass Aegis (8) — allies within Tier squares gain +Tier to every defense this round.

  • Sanctum (9) — immune to one damage type for a round.

  • Mythic Stand (10) — invulnerable until the start of your next turn.

These were always the Bulwark's birthright; they no longer leak into everyone else's menu. Frame Dice and Ruin Charges endure as the strategic layer — Catastrophic Entry still sunders armor and breaches structures, Ruin still cuts a Siege's cost — and both refill on a Soma Break.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
You no longer push against the world's resistances. They simply do not apply to you.

At Bulwark Initiation 16, both poles of your inevitability harden:

  • Ruin bypass. Damage you deal as part of any feature that explicitly spends a Ruin Charge ignores all kinetic-type resistance and any cover/structure damage-reduction the target would otherwise apply. (Energy/Sephirotic/etc. resistances still apply.)

  • Frame absorption. When a Frame Die you spend reduces incoming damage (per a doctrine feature or Tier 2 Anchor stance), reduce the incoming damage by an additional Violence value points before the Frame Die roll is added.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Nothing that stands can be moved. Your inevitability is the kind that absorbs.

Mode: Immovable Object / drift: Away.

You generate Ruin Charges by absorbing damage rather than by breaking things. Each time you take damage ≥ Violence value + Bulwark Initiation in a single instance and remain upright (Integrity > 0), gain 1 Ruin Charge. Maximum 1 Ruin Charge generated per turn from this feature.

End-of-scene conversion. Any Ruin Charges still in your pool when the scene ends convert 1-for-1 into Frame Dice on your next Soma Break (replacing the Frame Dice that would otherwise refill from the pool maximum, up to your Frame max).

system.requirements: Path of the Mountain, Bulwark Initiation 1

description.value:
"You belong here now. Argue with the mountain."

Doctrine: Durability, refusal, rootedness — immovable, load-bearing, patient.

The Mountain makes the scene bounce off you. Your Surge spends are the geometry of refusal: roots that share their footing, a flat "no" to the next thing done to you or yours, and a bastion the whole line forms behind.

Path (spent via Surge)

  • Root (1) — you and adjacent allies gain DR equal to Tier and cannot be forcibly moved.
  • Deny (2) — you or an ally becomes immune to forced-movement/CC and gains DR this round.
  • Bastion (5) — allies within Tier squares gain DR equal to Tier; you cannot be moved.

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Time itself counts as ground you have claimed.

You cannot be moved from a space you have occupied for at least one full round, except by a single damage instance equal to or greater than your current Integrity value. This denial covers, but is not limited to:

  • Forced movement of any kind (push, pull, slide, throw)

  • Teleportation effects targeting you

  • Banishment, dimensional swap, and plane-shift effects

  • Knockback from area-of-effect damage

  • Grapple and drag attempts

You may end the Hold voluntarily as a free action on your turn. After moving voluntarily, you must occupy a new space for one full round before the Hold protects you again.

system.requirements: Path of the Mountain, Bulwark Initiation 9

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, you choose which kind of inevitability you are.

Anchor or Advance — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As part of any action on your turn, declare a stance. The chosen stance lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Anchor. You cannot be moved against your will by any effect short of a Heroic-DC (22) push from a creature of your size or larger. Forced movement, knockback, teleportation targeting you, banishment, and dimensional swap effects all fail.

  • Advance. You cannot be prevented from reaching a destination you declare on the same action. Difficult terrain, conditions that halve speed, reaction strikes, and zone-of-control effects do not stop your movement toward that point. You may still take damage along the way.

Doctrine features at L5+ extend or modify which stance you favor.

description.value:
The world has two ways of saying no to change. You learn one of them today.

On gaining Bulwark Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Athletics (Violence).

  • Skill rank +1 in one tool of your choice (any single tool tracked as a skill on your sheet).

  • Violence marks cap +3 and Siege marks cap +2 on your Domain.

  • Your Frame Dice pool comes online (persistence — d8 dice, spend to absorb hits or fuel doctrine effects). Pool max = max(2, ceil((Violence value + Bulwark Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8.

  • Your Ruin Charges pool comes online (inevitability — single-use charges, spend to fuel offensive doctrine effects). Same pool-size formula.

Both pools refill on a Soma Break. How you generate them depends on your chosen Path; see your doctrine's L1 feature.

description.value:
"The first shape was softer. The second shape remembers."

The Thing You Were (1/Scene). Bonus action — briefly re-surface a trait of your pre-pressure self. Pick one of three options; it lasts until the end of your next turn:

  • Softer: your movement increases by 2 squares and you reroll the lowest die on Intrigue checks to squeeze or slip past.
  • Older: you gain low-light vision 12 squares if you don't already have it, or +6 squares if you do.
  • Wetter: you become immune to the Burning and Prone conditions, and difficult terrain does not slow you.

Each option refreshes on Soma Break — you cannot pick the same option twice before a Soma Break.

  • Heavy Presence. Your weight and settledness are perceptible. Creatures within 2 squares of you know you are there even if they cannot see you; you roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 on Intrigue (Stealth) checks unless you are on or in stone.

Metamorphic Traits

  • Pressure Remade. At the end of each Soma Break, the day chooses what you are until your next Soma Break. Roll a d4 or pick (GM discretion): (1) +1 Guard, (2) resistance to kinetic damage, (3) +1 rank on one skill of your choice, (4) reroll-lowest on Body checks to resist being knocked prone or grappled. You announce the result; you do not pre-pick.

  • Unbreakable Core. You reroll the lowest die on defense checks against petrification, forced transmutation, and forced shape-change. You have been turned into something else once already; nobody does it twice without your say-so.

Domain Edge

  • Domain Edge. Your Domain gains +20 Intrigue marks and +20 Non-Lethal marks at campaign start.

description.value:
Tier 1 — Mercenary Band

“We are not a problem. We are a subscription.”

Mercenary Bands turn violence into a service industry. They’re disciplined when paid, unpredictable when not, and always looking for the next contract that lets them keep their code while breaking yours.

You’re learning the shape of your shadow. Expect mistakes. Budget for them.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Plating and Melee.
  • Strategic: Your Domain's Violence marks cap rises by 10.

Tier 1 — Goetic Summoner

“First lesson: the circle protects you. Second lesson: only if it’s perfect.”

You learn the etiquette of predators: names, constraints, and the price of eye contact. You are not yet strong enough to command, but you are strong enough to be heard.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Occult and Intimidation
  • Learn Find Familiar, flavored as unsettling, watchful, or veil-adjacent

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • When your Domain attempts intimidation, coercion, or violent leverage, gain +1 to the relevant Violence marks roll
  • When your Domain runs reconnaissance, blackmail, or covert acquisition, gain +1 to the relevant Intrigue marks roll
  • When your Domain attempts goodwill, legitimacy, or mass Diplomacy, suffer –1 to the relevant Soft Power marks roll

Cost: early Goetic work leaves an obvious scent. Expect attention from the wrong entities, fear from the right people, and a reputation that arrives before you do.
